review_notes: I read the whole file and searched Mathlib for competing versions of its four constructions. (1) `Unitization.ringEquivProd`: Mathlib only has the additive/linear/type equivalences `Unitization.equiv`, `addEquiv` and the linear equivalence at Algebra/Algebra/Unitization.lean:290. The ring and algebra equivalences I found are for specific targets (C(OnePoint X, R), Algebra.adjoin), not for R × A. I found no ring equivalence from the unitization of a unital algebra to R × A, and this one uses a different, non-twisted multiplication. (2) `matrixRingEquivProd`: searches for matrix-over-product and matrix-product equivalences (prodMatrix, matrixProd, piMatrix, `Matrix n n (R × A)`) found nothing in Mathlib. (3) `unitizationGeneralLinearEquivProd` reuses Mathlib's `Units.mapEquiv` and `MulEquiv.prodUnits` rather than redefining them. (4) `nonUnitalGeneralLinearGroupEquiv` relates the file's own augmentation-kernel group to `GL`. Its source, `nonUnitalGeneralLinearGroup`, is defined in the sibling file `GeneralLinearGroups.NonUnitalNilpotent`, which I did not read. Because that definition is used on purpose for non-unital rings, and this file reconciles it with `GL` instead of adding a second version, I do not count it as a competing duplicate. Remaining uncertainty: I did not open the sibling file, so I did not check whether `nonUnitalGeneralLinearGroup` itself could be replaced by an existing Mathlib notion.
